faqs.question: What does AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Rifampicin measure?
faqs.answer: AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Rifampicin measures the drug susceptibility of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (the bacteria that causes TB) to the antibiotic Rifampicin.

faqs.question: Why is AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Rifampicin done?
faqs.answer: • To determine if Mycobacterium tuberculosis is resistant to Rifampicin, aiding in effective treatment selection • To assess the drug susceptibility pattern of TB to ensure appropriate and timely therapy • To monitor the emergence of drug resistance during TB treatment

faqs.question: When is AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Rifampicin recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test is recommended • when a patient is diagnosed with tuberculosis and needs drug susceptibility testing, • if a patient has previously been treated for tuberculosis but shows signs of recurrent or persistent infection, or • for patients at high risk of drug-resistant TB, such as those with a history of non-compliance with treatment or exposure to someone with drug-resistant TB.

faqs.question: What if the results of the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Rifampicin are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results may indicate resistance to Rifampicin, suggesting the need for alternative drug choices.

faqs.question: What to expect during the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Rifampicin?
faqs.answer: During this test, a healthcare professional will take a sample of your Tuberculosis bacteria. They will test this sample using the MGIT method to determine drug susceptibility.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Rifampicin?
faqs.answer: • Follow any instructions provided by your healthcare provider regarding dietary restrictions or medication adjustments. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Rifampicin?
faqs.answer: • AFB smear and culture: These tests are used to initially detect and identify Mycobacterium tuberculosis. • Genotypic testing: :ine probe assays or polymerase chain reaction (PCR) can identify specific genetic mutations associated with drug resistance.

faqs.question: What is AFB (TB) Antibiogram - Rifampicin also known as?
faqs.answer: TB drug susceptibility testing for Rifampicin or TB antibiotic sensitivity testing for Rifampicin

faqs.question: What is tuberculosis (TB)?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body.
